1.
Heard the learned counsel for respective sides.
2.  The petitioners are aggrieved by the order dated 21.07.2022 passed by the Land Acquisition Officer and Sub-Divisional Officer, Parli-Vaijinath, Dist. Beed.
By the said order, the petitioners' application for redetermination of compensation was rejected on the ground that it was not filed within the prescribed period of limitation.

3. The petitioners moved the application under Section 28-A the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 (for short, "the Act"), which mandates that the Land Acquisition Officer must redetermine the amount of compensation for other landholders covered by the same notification, based on an award enhanced by the Civil Court under Section 18 of Kaiser Anis Patel And Another vs The State Of Maharashtra Through ... on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150995094/
1 the Act.

sentences.text: It is an admitted fact that the petitioners were not parties to the Section 18 reference proceedings.

The counsel for the petitioners submits that the application was moved promptly upon obtaining knowledge of the same and therefore, the benefit of Section 28-A should not be denied on a narrow interpretation of limitation.
4. The learned counsel for Respondent No. 3 contends that the land of petitioners was not covered under the same notification as the reference land or that the reference was for a different purpose.

While these are substantive grounds that the respondents may raise during the hearing of the application on its merits, they do not justify a summary rejection at the threshold on the ground of limitation.

Since the petitioners were not parties to the reference, the Land Acquisition Officer erred in rejecting the application without a full inquiry into the date of knowledge and the applicability of the court award.
5. In view of the above, the Writ Petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 21.07.2022 passed by the Land Acquisition Officer and Sub-Divisional Officer, Parli-Vaijinath, Dist. Beed, is quashed and set aside.
6. It is clarified that this Court has not recorded any findings on the merits of the case.
All grounds remain open for the respondents to contest during the redetermination process.

7. However, to balance the equities, it is directed that in the event the Land Acquisition Officer enhances the compensation, the petitioners shall not be entitled to receive interest for the period from the date of the original rejection i.e. 21.07.2022 till today 04.03.2026.
8. Pending civil applications, if any, also stands disposed of.

(SIDDHESHWAR S. THOMBRE, J.) Omkar Joshi Kaiser Anis Patel And Another vs The State Of Maharashtra Through ... on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150995094/
